Introduced in 6fdcab9f for AKS observability. Advisory 1117943 (Prometheus exporter process crash via malformed HTTP request) is a DoS-class issue; the exporter is only reachable from inside the cluster (no public ingress to /metrics), so practical risk is low. Track upstream patch and upgrade when published.

Transitively flagged via the OpenTelemetry core/exporter DoS advisories (1117942, 1124011 — malformed trace/propagation header crashes). Removing them requires a breaking OpenTelemetry major upgrade (npm audit fix --force), tracked separately to avoid destabilising AKS telemetry init. Practical risk is low: propagators/exporters are internal and /metrics has no public ingress.

Advisory 1124011: JaegerPropagator DoS via unhandled exception on a malformed header. Fix is a breaking OpenTelemetry major upgrade (tracked with the sdk-node entry). Low practical risk — trace propagation is internal, no untrusted public trace headers are parsed.

fast-uri host-confusion advisories (1124015 IDN canonicalization; 1124064 literal backslash authority delimiter GHSA-v2hh-gcrm-f6hx; 1124231 failed IDN canonicalization GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6). GitHub re-issued/split the original advisory into the two new IDs; same vulnerability class and same transitive path (fastify/ajv URI parsing, range >=3.0.0 <=3.1.3). The only fix pulls a second fast-uri major that npm dedupe cannot collapse (dependency-duplication regression), so deferred to a batched dependency upgrade. Practical risk is low: URI parsing is not used for security-authority host decisions in our request path.

Advisory 1124282 (GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2): React Router RSC-mode CSRF bypass allowing action execution before a 400 response. The vulnerability is reachable only in React Router's RSC (React Server Components) framework mode; the Abbeygate frontend is a client-side Vite SPA using react-router-dom in library mode, so the affected server action pathway does not exist in our request path. No fixed release is published yet — latest 7.18.2 is still inside the affected 7.12.0-8.2.0 range and there is no 8.3.0 — so npm audit fix cannot remediate. Time-boxed; upgrade to the patched release when React Router ships it.

Transitively flagged because react-router-dom depends on the affected react-router range (advisory 1124282, RSC-mode CSRF). Same rationale as the react-router entry: client-side SPA usage does not exercise RSC mode, and no patched release exists. Tracked together with react-router.

Advisory 1139346 (GHSA extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal). CORRECTION (Codex P2, 2026-08-14): puppeteer IS a production dependency (backend PDF renderers backend/modules/documents/domain/renderers/pdfRenderer.ts and backend/products/motor/documents/pdfRenderer.ts launch Chromium at runtime), so the earlier 'dev/CI-only' claim was wrong. However, extract-zip is only reached by @puppeteer/browsers when it DOWNLOADS and unpacks a Chromium archive. Every production image disables that path: infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile, Dockerfile.api and Dockerfile.worker set PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 and PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD=1 and point PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH at the OS-provided /usr/bin/chromium (apt chromium). So extract-zip is never invoked in the deployed runtime and never touches the request path; the only time it runs at all is a developer running a local Chromium install, unpacking Google's own CDN archive (trusted input), which the symlink-traversal class does not affect. Residual production risk is nil. Time-boxed; drop when puppeteer ships a build depending on a patched extract-zip.

Transitively flagged via extract-zip (advisory 1139346). @puppeteer/browsers is puppeteer's browser-download helper; puppeteer ships in production but the download path is disabled in every image (PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 + PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD=1, OS chromium via PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH), so this helper never runs in the deployed runtime. Tracked with the extract-zip entry.

Not reached in the deployed runtime. Tracked with the extract-zip entry.
